findings.title: Proper eating, tasting, drinking, or tobacco use.
findings.comment: Inspector observed a cup with a straw and NO lid next to the sushi prep station. CORRECTED- the item was removed from the area before it could be addressed with staff. Ensure all beverages are covered with a lid and straw, and stored in a way to prevent contamination of items for service.
findings.citation_text: 2-401.11(B) Eating, Drinking, or Using TOBACCO PRODUCTS.(B) A FOOD EMPLOYEE may drink from a closed BEVERAGE container if the container is handled to prevent contamination of: (1) The EMPLOYEE'S hands; (2) The container; and (3) Exposed FOOD; clean EQUIPMENT, UTENSILS, and LINENS; and unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES.[C]

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed.
findings.comment:
Inspector observed multiple instances of incorrect hand washing:
1) An employee was observed to wash hands, and use their bare hands to turn off the faucet. CORRECTED- education was provided. Ensure the use of a barrier to prevent re-contaminating hands.
2) An employee was observed to be washing hands with gloved hands. CORRECTED- the hand washing was halted, gloves were removed, hands were rewashed, and a paper towel was used to turn off the faucet.
Frequently review hand washing with all staff.
findings.citation_text: 2-301.12(B) Cleaning Procedure. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall use the following cleaning procedure in the order stated to clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms, including surrogate prosthetic devices for hands and arms: (1) Rinse under clean, running warm water; (2) Apply an amount of cleaning compound recommended by the cleaning compound manufacturer; (3) Rub together vigorously for at least 10 to 15 seconds while: (a) Paying particular attention to removing soil from underneath the fingernails during the cleaning procedure, and (b) Creating friction on the surfaces of the hands and arms or surrogate prosthetic devices for hands and arms, finger tips, and areas between the fingers; (4) Thoroughly rinse under clean, running warm water; and (5) Immediately follow the cleaning procedure with thorough drying using a method as specified under § 6-301.12. [P]

findings.title: Food in good condition, safe, and unadulterated.
findings.comment: Inspectors observed foods listed as “white tuna” on the tablet menu for customers. On the letter of parasite destruction, it was observed the facility orders “Escolar”, which is not the same species as “white tuna.” According to the FDA, Escolar (Lepidocybium flavobrunneum) is not to be sold under the name white tuna. Acceptable market names for this fish are escolar or oilfish. White tuna refers to albacore tuna (Thunnus alalunga). CORRECTED- PIC changed the electronic menus to list escolar properly. Ensure that foods are labeled as ordered to prevent misbranding.
findings.citation_text: 3-101.11 Safe, Unadulterated, and Honestly Presented. FOOD shall be safe, unADULTERATED, and, as specified under § 3-601.12, honestly presented. [P]

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: SECOND REPEAT: The facility’s dish machine was run multiple times and each time was observed to have a sanitizing concentration of 0 ppm. The PIC primed the sanitizer multiple times, until it was observed to be dispensing 50 ppm Cl. However, after several regular wash cycles, the sanitizer concentration was again observed at 0ppm Cl. PIC confirmed that a technician would be out to service the machine to ensure it is reaching a sanitizer concentration of 50-200ppm Cl. The facility should use test strips at least ONCE A DAY to ensure that the dish machine is reaching proper sanitizing concentrations (50-200 ppm Chlorine bleach). Recommended maintaining logs or other documentation of daily dish machine checks.
findings.citation_text: 4-501.114(A) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (A) A chlorine solution shall have a minimum temperature based on the concentration and PH of the solution as listed in the chart in 4-501.114 (A). [P]

findings.title: Approved thawing methods used.
findings.comment: Inspector observed an unopened package of vacuum sealed tuna thawing in the sushi prep cooler. CORRECTED- item was removed from packaging to thaw. Ensure items in reduced oxygen packaging are vented when moved to thaw to prevent the potential for Botulism growth.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.13(E) Thawing. Except as specified in (D) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be thawed: (E) REDUCED OXYGEN PACKAGED FISH that bears a label indicating that it is to be kept frozen until time of use shall be removed from the reduced oxygen environment: (1) Prior to its thawing under refrigeration as specified in (A) of this section; or (2) Prior to, or Immediately upon completion of, its thawing using procedures specified in (B) of this section.[Pf]

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment:
Inspector observed multiple areas within the physical facilities in need of repair:
1) The floor drain below the dish machine was lacking a drain grate. CORRECTED- a grate was placed.
2) The door and floor of the walk in freezer are peeling, exposing insulation (as a result of routinely removing ice from the freezer). Ensure floor and door are repaired by the next routine inspection. Nonfood contact surfaces should be smooth and easily cleanable.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair. [C]

findings.title: Food separated and protected.
findings.comment:
Inspectors observed multiple incidents of incorrect storage order:
1) FIRST REPEAT- raw shrimp over unwashed vegetables in the walk in cooler.
2) Raw beef over edamame in the grill prep cooler.
CORRECTED- the shrimp was moved above raw beef in the walk in, and the edamame was moved above the beef in the prep cooler. Ensure all foods are stored in a manner that prevents contamination (top-> bottom= ready-to eat, washed produce, unwashed produce, seafood (145), whole beef (145F), ground beef (155F), chicken (165F).
findings.citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(1) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (1) Except as specified in (1)(d) below or when combined as ingredients, separating raw animal FOODS during storage, preparation, holding, and display from: (a) Raw READY-TO-EAT FOOD including other raw animal FOOD such as FISH for sushi or MOLLUSCAN SHELLFISH, or other raw READY-TOEAT FOOD such as fruits and vegetables, (b) Cooked READY-TO-EAT FOOD, and (c) Fruits and vegetables before they are washed; (d) Frozen, commercially processed and packaged raw animal FOOD may be stored or displayed with or above frozen, commercially processed and packaged, ready-to-eat food.[P]

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: Inspectors observed an accumulation of biofilm on the soda nozzles at the server station, as well as the soda gun holder at the bar. CORRECTED- items were removed for proper ware washing. Discussed increasing the frequency at which the nozzles are cleaned, and use a brush to remove debris moving forward. Ensure all foods are maintained clean to sight and touch.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. [Pf]

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: FIRST REPEAT: The facility’s dish machine was run over 5 times and each time was observed to have a sanitizing concentration of 0 ppm. The sanitizer was primed and the bucket was replaced before the PIC called their service provider to have the machine serviced. CORRECTED- While the inspector was writing the report the service provider was able to examine the machine and verify that the dish machine was reaching the appropriate sanitizing concentration (100 ppm). Facility should use test strips at least ONCE A DAY to ensure that the dish machine is reaching proper sanitizing concentrations.
findings.citation_text: 4-501.114(A) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (A) A chlorine solution shall have a minimum temperature based on the concentration and PH of the solution as listed in the chart in 4-501.114 (A). [P]

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
findings.comment:
Inspectors observed soup dumplings stored in a styrofoam container in the standing freezer. CORRECTED- the PIC moved the food into a food grade container. Do not store food into containers that cannot withstand warewashing.

4-101.11(B)-(E) Characteristics. Materials that are used in the construction of UTENSILS and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT may not allow the migration of deleterious substances or impart colors, odors, or tastes to FOOD and under normal use conditions shall be: (B) Durable, CORROSION-RESISTANT, and nonabsorbent; (C) Sufficient in weight and thickness to withstand repeated WAREWASHING; (D) Finished to have a SMOOTH, EASILY CLEANABLE surface; and (E) Resistant to pitting, chipping, crazing, scratching, scoring, distortion, and decomposition. [C]

findings.title: No bare-hand contact with RTE food or a pre-approved alternative procedure properly allowed.
findings.comment:
FIRST REPEAT: Inspectors observed multiple soup containers being reused as scoops in ready to eat (RTE) foods (including but not limited to a sushi vinegar marinade and sugar). CORRECTED- the PIC removed the soup containers and replaced them with scoops with handles. Any utensils used with RTE foods must have a food contact surface as well as a hand contact surface to prevent bare hand contamination of food. 
* This violation was previously noted as violation #43 during the last routine inspection, and has since been moved to #9.*
findings.citation_text: 3-301.11(B) Preventing Contamination from Hands. (B) Except when washing fruits and vegetables as specified under §3-302.15 or as specified in (D) and (E) of this section, FOOD EMPLOYEES may not contact exposed, READY-TO-EAT FOOD with their bare hands and shall use suitable UTENSILS such as deli tissue, spatulas, tongs, single-use gloves, or dispensing EQUIPMENT. [P]

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
findings.comment: FIRST REPEAT: Inspector observed 2 sponges and 1 steel wool in the basin of the hand washing sink near the West sushi prep station. The person in charge (PIC) indicated that the sponges are at the sink to clean the sink. CORRECTED- the PIC moved the sponges and steel wool to the dish area. If sponges are used to clean the sink they should ONLY be brought over for that purpose and then immediately returned to the dish area. All hand washing sinks should be used for hand washing only. Using hand washing sinks for other purposes may deter hand washing for food handlers.
findings.citation_text: 5-205.11 Using a Handwashing Sink. (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. (C) An automatic handwashing facility shall be used in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions. [Pf]

findings.title: Food separated and protected.
findings.comment: Inspector observed improper storage order in the facility’s walk in cooler. Shrimp was stored over vegetables- including but not limited to jalapeños. CORRECTED- the PIC rearranged ready to eat (RTE) food items to be stored over animal proteins. Inspector gave PIC storage order handouts in English, Spanish, and Mandarin to be hung around the facility. Ensure RTE food items are always stored above animal proteins, and animal proteins are stored by increasing internal cooking temperatures (items with the highest internal cooking temperatures should be stored at the bottom) to prevent cross contamination.
findings.citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(1) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (1) Except as specified in (1)(d) below or when combined as ingredients, separating raw animal FOODS during storage, preparation, holding, and display from: (a) Raw READY-TO-EAT FOOD including other raw animal FOOD such as FISH for sushi or MOLLUSCAN SHELLFISH, or other raw READY-TOEAT FOOD such as fruits and vegetables, (b) Cooked READY-TO-EAT FOOD, and (c) Fruits and vegetables before they are washed; (d) Frozen, commercially processed and packaged raw animal FOOD may be stored or displayed with or above frozen, commercially processed and packaged, ready-to-eat food. [P]

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: The facility’s dish machine was run 3 separate times and each time was observed to have a sanitizing concentration of 0 ppm. The PIC called their service provider to have the machine serviced. CORRECTED- While the inspector was writing the report the service provider was able to examine the machine and verify that the dish machine was reaching the appropriate sanitizing concentration (200 ppm). Facility should use test strips at least once a day to ensure that the dish machine is reaching proper sanitizing concentrations.
findings.citation_text: 4-501.114(A) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (A) A chlorine solution shall have a minimum temperature based on the concentration and PH of the solution as listed in the chart in 4-501.114 (A). [P]

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: FIRST REPEAT: Inspector observed no measurable concentration of sanitizer at the rotary bar sanitation bucket. CORRECTED- the sanitizer bucket was remade to have a concentration of 200 ppm Cl. Ensure sanitizer buckets are made and checked (with the facility’s test strips) at a frequency to contain the correct concentration of sanitizer as recommended by the manufacturer's label.
findings.citation_text: 4-501.114(A) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (A) A chlorine solution shall have a minimum temperature based on the concentration and PH of the solution as listed in the chart in 4-501.114 (A). [P]

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition.
findings.comment: Inspector observed items in the dessert cooler to be marked with times of preparation which had not passed yet (12:30pm time observed at 11:20am). The PIC indicated that the items were prepared at that time the day before. CORRECTED- the desserts were also labeled with the day they were prepared. Ensure all Time and Temperature Control for Food Safety (TCS) items being held for more than one day are marked with the day of preparation or thawing.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.18(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Disposition. (A) A FOOD specified in 3-501.17(A) or (B) shall be discarded if it: (1) Exceeds the temperature and time combination specified in 3-501.17(A), except time that the product is frozen; (2) Is in a container or PACKAGE that does not bear a date or day; or (3) Is inappropriately marked with a date or day that exceeds a temperature and time combination as specified in 3-501.17(A). [P]

findings.title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored.
findings.comment: Inspectors observed multiple incidents of wet sanitizing cloths being stored on the counters of food preparation areas. CORRECTED- the wet cloths were moved to a sanitizer bucket. Ensure sanitizing cloths are stored in a sanitizer bucket in between use to prevent the growth and harborage of microorganisms.
findings.citation_text: 3-304.14(B) Wiping Cloths, Use Limitation. (B) Cloths in-use for wiping counters and other EQUIPMENT surfaces shall be: (1) Held between uses in a chemical sanitizer solution at a concentration specified under § 4-501.114; and (2) Laundered daily as specified under 4-802.11(D).[C]

findings.title: Plumbing installed; proper backflow devices.
findings.comment: FIRST REPEAT: Inspector observed a leak from base of the faucet at the hand washing sink behind the West sushi station. CORRECTED-The sink was removed from the wall to tighten the fitting during the inspection. Ensure that all plumbing systems at the facility are maintained in good repair.
findings.citation_text: 5-205.15(B) System Maintained in Good Repair. A plumbing system shall be: (B) Maintained in good repair. [C]

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed.
findings.comment: Inspector observed an employee turn off the hand washing sink faucet using their bare hands. CORRECTED- the person in charge (PIC) demonstrated how to correctly wash hands, and had that employee re-wash their hands correctly. Ensure ongoing education on proper handwashing occurs- including using a barrier to turn off the faucet to prevent food handlers from re-contaminating their hands.
findings.citation_text: 2-301.12(C) Cleaning Procedure. (C) To avoid recontaminating their hands or surrogate prosthetic devices, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use disposable paper towels or similar clean barriers when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a HANDWASHING SINK or the handle of a restroom door. [C]

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
findings.comment: Inspector observed the handwashing sink at the bar to be out of paper towels. CORRECTED- PIC replaced paper towels. Ensure all sinks designated for handwashing are always supplied with warm running water, soap, and paper towels.
findings.citation_text: 6-301.12 Hand Drying Provision. Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with: (A) Individual, disposable towels; (B) A continuous towel system that supplies the user with a clean towel; or (C) A heated-air hand drying device; or (D) A hand drying device that employs an air-knife system that delivers high velocity, pressurized air at ambient temperatures. [Pf]

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
findings.comment: Inspector observed an employee washing utensils at a hand sink. CORRECTED- the PIC had the utensils moved to the dish area and reminded the employee to use hand washing sinks for hand washing only. Ensure continuous education occurs among staff. Sinks designated for hand washing are to be used for hand washing only- to ensure accessibility for hand washing.
findings.citation_text: 5-205.11 Using a Handwashing Sink. (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. [Pf]

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: Inspector observed no measurable concentration of sanitizer at the server station sanitation bucket. CORRECTED- the sanitizer bucket was remade to have a concentration of 200 ppm Cl. Ensure sanitizer buckets are made and checked (with the facility’s test strips) at a frequency to contain the correct concentration of sanitizer as recommended by the manufacturer's label.
findings.citation_text: 4-501.114(A) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (A) A chlorine solution shall have a minimum temperature based on the concentration and PH of the solution as listed in the chart in 4-501.114 (A). [P]

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition.
findings.comment: Inspector observed open containers of milk and orange juice at the bar without date marking. CORRECTED- The PIC stated the items were opened yesterday and labeled them accordingly. Ensure temperature control for safety (TCS) foods being held over 24 hours are labeled with the date they are opened, and are used or discarded within 7 days.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.17(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. (A) Except when PACKAGING FOOD using a REDUCED OXYGEN PACKAGING method as specified under § 3-502.12, and except as specified in (E) and (F) of this section, refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and held in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature of 5C (41F) or less for a maximum of 7 days. The day of preparation shall be counted as Day 1. [Pf]

findings.title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored and used.
findings.comment: A spray bottle of clean linen air freshener was observed over clean plates next to the sushi station (nearest the restrooms). CORRECTED- PIC removed the spray bottle from the kitchen. Ensure chemicals are clearly identified and stored away from and under food or food contact surfaces to avoid contaminating food.
findings.citation_text: 7-201.11 Separation. Poisonous or toxic materials shall be stored so they can not contaminate food, equipment, utensils, linens, and single-service and single-use articles by: (B) Locating the POISONOUS OR TOXIC MATERIALS in an area that is not above FOOD, EQUIPMENT, UTENSILS, LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE or SINGLE-USE ARTICLES. [P]

findings.title: Thermometers are provided and accurate.
findings.comment: When asked, the PIC indicated that there were no probe thermometers present in the facility. CORRECTED- A second PIC brought two probe thermometers to be used within the facility. Inspector demonstrated thermometer calibration using the ice water method. Ensure probe thermometers are available and calibrated to measure the internal temperatures of TCS foods.
findings.citation_text: 4-203.11 Temperature Measuring Devices, Food. (A) FOOD TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICES that are scaled only in Celsius or dually scaled in Celsius and Fahrenheit shall be accurate to ±1°C in the intended range of use. (B) FOOD TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICES that are scaled only in Fahrenheit shall be accurate to ±2°F in the intended range of use. [Pf]

findings.title: Food properly labeled; original container.
findings.comment: Inspector observed three (two in dry storage, and one over the prep cooler on the cook line) containers of white powders lacking a label. CORRECTED- the PIC labeled the items as sugar and salt. Ensure items that may be easily mistaken for other items are labeled with their name to avoid potential contamination of food.
findings.citation_text: 3-302.12 Food Storage Containers, Identified with Common Name of Food. Except for containers holding FOOD that can be readily and unmistakably recognized such as dry pasta, working containers holding FOOD or FOOD ingredients that are removed from their original packages for use in the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT, such as cooking oils, flour, herbs, potato flakes, salt, spices, and sugar shall be identified with the common name of the FOOD. [C]

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
findings.comment: Inspector observed fly strips hanging throughout areas of food preparation in the kitchen. CORRECTED- PIC had kitchen staff remove the fly strips. Ensure insect control devices are not located over areas of food preparation to prevent contamination of food.
findings.citation_text: 6-202.13 Insect Control Devices, Design and Installation. (B) Insect control devices shall be installed so that: (1) The devices are not located over a FOOD preparation area; and (2) Dead insects and insect fragments are prevented from being impelled onto or falling on exposed FOOD; clean EQUIPMENT, UTENSILS, and LINENS; and unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES. [C]

findings.title: In-use utensils: properly stored.
findings.comment:
Inspector observed multiple instances of improper in-use utensil storage:
1) Soup containers were being used as scoops submerged in soy sauce and sugar containers. CORRECTED- PIC removed the containers or replaced them with a ladle. There is no clear hand contact surface on soup containers, which poses a risk of bare hand contamination of food.
2) The handle of the ice scoop at the server station was touching ice. CORRECTED- PIC removed the ice and placed the ice scoop in a cup. 

Ensure ready to eat (RTE) food items (that require no further processing or cooking) contain scoops with handles. Ensure the handle is sticking outward and the food contact surface is in the food to prevent cross contamination from bare hand contact.
findings.citation_text: 3-304.12(A) In-Use Utensils, Between-Use Storage. During pauses in FOOD preparation or dispensing, FOOD preparation and dispensing UTENSILS shall be stored: (A) Except as specified under (B) of this section, in the food with their handles above the top of the food and the container. [C]

findings.title: Plumbing installed; proper backflow devices.
findings.comment: Inspector observed leaks from base of two faucets in the kitchen (on the cookline and in the dish area). Per discussion with PICs, the sinks will need to be removed from the wall to tighten the fitting. See that the leaks are repaired by the next routine inspection.
findings.citation_text: 5-205.15(B) System Maintained in Good Repair. A plumbing system shall be: (B) Maintained in good repair. [C]

findings.title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used.
findings.comment: Multiple personal items, such as personal drinks, personal food, hats, and first aid supplies were observed throughout the kitchen during today’s inspection. CORRECTED- PIC moved the personal items to an area away from food for service. Inspector recommends setting a designated space for personal items that is separate and below foods intended for service, to protect foods for service from contamination.
findings.citation_text: 6-403.11(A) Designated Areas. (A) Areas designated for EMPLOYEES to eat, drink, and use TOBACCO PRODUCTS shall be located so that FOOD, EQUIPMENT, LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES are protected from contamination. [C]

findings.title: Food handler training
findings.comment:
Inspector observed more food handlers at the facility than there are food handler certificates (inspector was provided with 4 food handler’s cards). All kitchen staff, bar tenders, and wait staff are required to obtain a food handler’s card within 30 days of hire. Ensure all employees have a food handler’s card by the next routine inspection.

410 ILCS 625/3.06(b). Food handler training: restaurants. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all food handlers employed by a restaurant, other than someone holding a food service sanitation manager certificate, must receive or obtain American National Standards Institute-accredited training in basic safe food handling principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Notwithstanding the provisions of Section 3.05 of this Act, food handlers employed in nursing homes, licensed day care homes and facilities, hospitals, schools, and long-term care facilities must renew their training every 3 years. There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training. The training indicated in subsections (e) and (f) of this Section is transferable between employers, but not individuals. The training indicated in subsections (c) and (d) of this Section is not transferable between individuals or employers. Proof that a food handler has been trained must be available upon reasonable request by a State or local health department inspector and may be provided electronically. [C]

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed.
findings.comment: A food employee was observed to rinse their gloved hands at the cookline handsink. This is not adequate handwashing procedure. Gloves are not intended to be washed. Employees must remove gloves to wash hands. CORRECTED- Discussed with PIC who provided education to the employee. Review proper handwashing procedure with all employees.
findings.citation_text: 2-301.12(B) Cleaning Procedure. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall use the following cleaning procedure in the order stated to clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms, including surrogate prosthetic devices for hands and arms: (1) Rinse under clean, running warm water; (2) Apply an amount of cleaning compound recommended by the cleaning compound manufacturer; (3) Rub together vigorously for at least 10 to 15 seconds while: (a) Paying particular attention to removing soil from underneath the fingernails during the cleaning procedure, and (b) Creating friction on the surfaces of the hands and arms or surrogate prosthetic devices for hands and arms, finger tips, and areas between the fingers; (4) Thoroughly rinse under clean, running warm water; and (5) Immediately follow the cleaning procedure with thorough drying using a method as specified under § 6-301.12. [P]

findings.title: No bare-hand contact with RTE food or a pre-approved alternative procedure properly allowed.
findings.comment: An employee was observed returning an edamame pod that had fallen from a dish onto a tray with their bare hands. CORRECTED- The container of edamame was voluntarily discarded. Discussed bare-hand contact with PIC who provided education to the employee. Employees need to use clean gloved hands or utensils to prevent bare hand contact when handling ready-to-eat foods.
findings.citation_text: 3-301.11(B) Preventing Contamination from Hands. (B) Except when washing fruits and vegetables as specified under §3-302.15 or as specified in (D) and (E) of this section, FOOD EMPLOYEES may not contact exposed, READY-TO-EAT FOOD with their bare hands and shall use suitable UTENSILS such as deli tissue, spatulas, tongs, single-use gloves, or dispensing EQUIPMENT. [P]

findings.title: Proper hot holding temperatures.
findings.comment: Foods at the sushi station heat lamp were observed below 135F: ribeye at 88F, eel at 130F, and eel at 98F, all probed. CORRECTED- Foods were cooked 1 hour prior and were allowed to be reheated to 165F before hot holding at 135F or above. For the heat lamp to work properly, foods need to be in a single layer directly under the lamp (not stacked or adjacent to the lamp). Moving forward, time as a control will be used to ensure that these foods are maintained safely. See General Comments for Time as a Control policy details.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(1) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained: (1) At 57°C (135°F) or above, except that roasts cooked to a temperature and for a time specified in 3-401.11(B) or reheated as specified in 3-403.11(E) may be held at a temperature of 54°C (130°F) or above. [P]

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
findings.comment: Kewpie mayo and other sauces were observed stored at room temperature at the sushi station. The sauce original containers bear labels instructing refrigeration after opening. CORRECTED- Discussed with PIC, who will ensure sauces are stored properly, including under refrigeration if the label instructs.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less. [P]

findings.title: Approved thawing methods used.
findings.comment: A bowl of thawed still-sealed packages of tuna were observed in the walk-in cooler. CORRECTED- Inspector provided education and discussed with PIC who will educate staff. ROP fish needs to be removed from the reduced oxygen environment (by cutting the packaging, for example) before thawing. PIC had an employee open the thawed packages. Ensure packages are cut prior to thawing.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.13(E) Thawing. REDUCED OXYGEN PACKAGED FISH that bears a label indicating that it is to be kept frozen until time of use shall be removed from the reduced oxygen environment: (1) Prior to its thawing under refrigeration as specified in (A) of this section; or (2) Prior to, or Immediately upon completion of, its thawing using procedures specified in (B) of this section. [Pf]

findings.title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored.
findings.comment: Two wet wiping cloths were observed stored on the sushi station cutting board. Ensure wet wiping cloths are stored submerged in sanitizer solution between uses.
findings.citation_text: 3-304.14(B) Wiping Cloths, Use Limitation. (B) Cloths in-use for wiping counters and other EQUIPMENT surfaces shall be: (1) Held between uses in a chemical sanitizer solution at a concentration specified under § 4-501.114; and (2) Laundered daily as specified under 4-802.11(D). [C]

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment: The sushi station handwashing sink is not sealed to the wall and needs to be re-caulked.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair. [C]
